3	Management, authoring, rendering and filling for questionnaires. Authoring
4	mounts at `/admin/questionnaires` and
5	`/facility/{id}/settings/questionnaires`; the fill experience mounts on the
6	encounter/patient questionnaire routes (`ConsultationRoutes.tsx`). It

9	`QuestionRenderer`, `QuestionInput` and the simple input components) is

14	(`form/engine/`). If you find yourself writing a second display path for
15	questions, that is the bug.

18

20	  (`questionnaireFormSchema.ts`) and the save mutation
21	  (`useUpdateQuestionnaire.ts`).
22	- `builder/` — the edit model the studio runs on: `builderReducer.ts` is
23	  the single source of edit state (a `Question[]` tree + selection + dirty

25	  `saveValidation.ts`. The editor cards (type picker, options, behaviour,

27	  the old page shell is gone (the routes mount `studio/`).

29	  left outline, live canvas (rendered by `form/`), right inspector. May
30	  import from `builder/` (model + cards), `manage/` (metadata form

32	- `form/` — the renderer (`QuestionnaireFormRenderer`): the whole
33	  questionnaire on one scroll, live-synced per-instance store (edits merge
34	  into responses instead of wiping them), a chrome/decoration seam for the
35	  studio canvas and the fill page's width policy, and the fill seams
36	  (`validation.ts`, mode union, creation-time `initialResponses`).
37	  - `form/engine/` — the headless half every host shares: the jotai store
38	    and enable_when resolution (`store.ts`), the type→component map
39	    (`questionTypeRegistry.tsx`), the inputs (`inputs/`, host-layout-free
40	    — each control carries its own full border), the class sanitizer

52	  host↔engine surface is that one callback. `submit/` is the errorsAtom
53	  writer: pure `composeBatch` (structured requests from the registry + the

56	  mapping routed back to the owning form's store. `draft/` is the local
57	  autosave layer: one localStorage entry per user/subject/entry

The QuestionnaireV2 fill page outline follows Figma node 43604-21509 in "Care - Master" (frame 43607:22081 = expanded overlay, 43607:22816 = collapsed): a ~24px tick rail (gray-400 hairlines, active tick 24px indigo-600) always at the canvas' left edge, and a 320px `bg-white/90 border-r shadow-lg` panel that floats OVER the full-width canvas. Implemented 2026-08-03 in `fill/FillOutlineOverlay.tsx` (+ `FillOutline.tsx`, `FillOutlineRail.tsx`).

**Why:** hover/focus/click opens; native `pointerenter/leave` listeners on the shell (NOT React's `onPointerEnter` — React's synthesized enter/leave never fired in the Claude in-app browser, and native works everywhere). Mouse clicks on an already-open rail are a no-op (hover governs mice; toggle-close is for touch/keyboard — see `clickPointerTypeRef`). Scroll-spy = rAF-throttled scroll listener picking the last `[data-question-id]` above a 96px line. Rail ticks carry `data-question-tick`/`data-active` for Playwright.

---
name: reference-browser-tool-quirks
description: Claude in-app Browser pane quirks — coordinate scale is displayed-image/2, React synthetic pointerenter doesn't fire
metadata:

---

Claude Code in-app Browser pane (mcp__Claude_Browser__computer):
- Screenshot coordinate space is the reported "Screenshot size" (e.g. 800x450); the rendered image you see is 2x that. **Divide visually-estimated pixel positions by 2** before clicking, or clicks land out of bounds and silently do nothing.
- Real DOM `pointerenter/pointerleave/pointerover` events fire (pointerType "mouse"), but **React's synthesized `onPointerEnter`/`onPointerLeave` handlers do not run** in this browser. Components needing hover must attach native listeners via refs (Playwright and real Chrome deliver both paths).
- State reads via `javascript_tool` right after a dispatched click can race React's async flush — re-read before concluding a handler didn't run.

All four parts are done and verified. Here's the summary.

## 1. Figma left nav — implemented as an overlay, not a fixed column

I pulled the design from Figma (node 43604-21509): the outline no longer reserves a 288px column. What ships, in three new/rewritten files ([FillOutlineOverlay.tsx](src/components/QuestionnaireV2/fill/FillOutlineOverlay.tsx), [FillOutline.tsx](src/components/QuestionnaireV2/fill/FillOutline.tsx), [FillOutlineRail.tsx](src/components/QuestionnaireV2/fill/FillOutlineRail.tsx)):

- A slim **tick rail** on the canvas' left edge — one hairline per visible top-level question (gray-400, active one longer and indigo-600, exactly the design's minimap), distributed over the rail height so long questionnaires never clip.
- The **320px panel floats over the full-width canvas** on hover, focus, or click (`bg-white/90`, right border, shadow-lg, per the design), with numbered rows, CheckCheck/Dot completion icons, indigo active row with the right-edge bar, and indented group children.
- **Scroll-spy** tracks the question in view; clicking a row scrolls to it and pins it active until the user scrolls. Multi-form sessions portal each form's rows and ticks into the shared overlay, keeping per-form stores intact.
- Verified live against the local backend; two hard-won correctness details: the overlay's dismissal handling uses **native DOM listeners** (portaled rows don't propagate React synthetic events through the overlay), and mouse/touch/keyboard each get a coherent open/close model (hover governs mice, tap toggles, focus+Escape for keyboard).

## 2. State management / data flow / submit review

A 20-agent adversarial review confirmed 15 real defects; I fixed 13 (1 refuted, 1 deferred as a chip). Highlights: a **critical** one where any background refetch of a resumed server draft unmounted the whole session destroying typed answers (`isFetching` → `isLoading`); render-failed structured questions were skipped by validation but **still composed and submitted unvalidated** (compose now shares the skip, and recovered slots un-mark themselves); a double-submit window while async compose ran; repeats answers dropping later rows when row 1 was cleared in place; a submitted `form_submission` resuming as an editable draft; and four draft-layer data-loss paths (Resume's fetch window, Discard destroying un-persisted typing, re-adding a drafted form, resume-collision with a hand-added form).

## 3. Production-quality UI review

A second 25-agent review confirmed 18 findings; I fixed 15: forward-Tab now reaches the open panel, `aria-required` on every input (the asterisk was visual-only), date/dateTime pickers get accessible names, keyboard row-activation moves focus to the question, Save Changes gets a pending spinner and primary-token styling (was hard-coded emerald), tab strip and action band no longer clip on phones, the loading skeleton uses the real fullscreen shell with a close button, encounter/patient fetch failures now show an error page instead of a headerless clinical form, and reduced-motion is respected. Deferred: the short-viewport header stack (rare viewport, needs a design call).

## 4. Playwright coverage

New [fillOutlineNav.spec.ts](tests/facility/patient/encounter/fill/fillOutlineNav.spec.ts) (15 tests: collapsed default, full-width canvas, tick counts, hover/click/focus/Escape, scroll-spy, completion icons, enable_when reveal, group children, multi-form sections) plus regression tests for the state fixes in the autosave, multi-form, server-draft and fill-page specs. No new backend fixtures were needed — the kitchen-sink fixture covers it. I also root-caused two pre-existing failures: the patient-subject spec's slug truncated `Date.now()` to a constant that collides with a record baked into the DB snapshot (fixed the spec), and the backend 500s on duplicate slugs (chip filed).

**Final state:** lint, prettier, and `tsc` clean; production build green; the full fill-related suite (fill, outline, structured, resource mounts) passes — 46/46 in my scope, with 2 skips (server-draft tests, gated on the `REACT_ENABLE_QUESTIONNAIRE_DRAFT` build flag) and one pre-existing flake in `diagnosis.spec.ts` that fails on a different test each run (chip filed).
